question: We're leaving the settlement to hunt a level 1 White Lion for the first time. How do we prepare the hunt board and advance through movement and events until the showdown starts?

record.title: Hunt board setup and event sequence

record.layout: Printed page 61 has the board setup list. Page 62 starts Hunt Your Quarry at the bottom left and continues at the top center; the percentile explanation continues from bottom center to top right. The White Lion story event supplies its hunt placement diagram.
record.summary: Choose an available quarry and level, then use its story-event hunt diagram to set up the hunt board. Shuffle monster hunt events onto E spaces, fill other eligible spaces with basic hunt event cards, place the monster at its level marker and survivors at Start. Survivors take turns revealing and resolving the events in their current space before advancing one space toward the monster.
notes: The board has 13 spaces. Do not put basic hunt event cards on monster-event spaces, Start, Overwhelming Darkness, or Starvation. Place any hunt events triggered by gear according to their rules.

The event revealer reads and resolves the top card in the survivors' space. After completing it, archive that card and pass revealer duty to the next survivor. Resolve stacked events one at a time from top to bottom before moving, unless an event compels movement.
When no cards remain in the current space, move one space toward the monster and resolve the top event in the new space. The monster stays still unless an event moves it.

An empty entered space requires a hunt-event-table roll before moving again, unless instructed to skip spaces. The first landing on Overwhelming Darkness during each hunt triggers that story event instead of a hunt-table roll.

Moving into the monster's space ends the hunt and starts the showdown immediately. Do not resolve hunt events in its space except Starvation. The Starvation and Overwhelming Darkness event effects are not included here.

A basic Random Event card directs a 1d100 hunt-event-table roll: roll two d10s, designate tens and ones, and combine them. The pictured example uses tens 3 and ones 5 for event 35. This record provides the procedure, not the 100 event outcomes.

An event specifies who rolls. If no survivor is specified, the event revealer rolls and makes required random choices. Add gathering events only with the appropriate tools, once per hunt per event, on top of existing cards and outside Start, Overwhelming Darkness, and Starvation.

Related reviewed rules:
Hunt event damage and explicit injuries: Ordinary hunt-event damage is nonlethal: it reduces armor or insanity and can fill light and heavy injury boxes, but does not cause severe injuries or brain trauma. This damage persists into the showdown. An event can explicitly instruct a severe injury or brain trauma; follow that instruction when present.

related_records.layout: Printed page 63 has Event Damage at the bottom of the left column. Its token-duration paragraph continues at the top of the center column, immediately before Severe Injuries and Brain Trauma. Those two headings form the hunt-specific rule unit. related_records.summary: Ordinary hunt-event damage is nonlethal: it reduces armor or insanity and can fill light and heavy injury boxes, but does not cause severe injuries or brain trauma. This damage persists into the showdown. An event can explicitly instruct a severe injury or brain trauma; follow that instruction when present.
notes: For damage to a physical location, reduce armor at that location to zero, then fill its available injury boxes in order: light, then heavy. Each point removes one armor point or fills one available box. Boxes already checked cannot absorb damage again. Any remaining ordinary hunt-event damage causes no severe injury.

Insanity protects only the brain. Physical damage to the body, head, arms, waist, or legs does not reduce insanity. Brain damage reduces insanity first, then fills the brain injury box. Remaining ordinary hunt-event brain damage causes no brain trauma.

State any assumption about existing injury boxes. With both body injury boxes empty, 3 body damage against 1 body armor removes that armor and fills both boxes. If either box is already checked, fill only the remaining available box; the hunt-event exception still prevents a severe injury. Insanity is unchanged by this body damage.
Tokens gained during the hunt remain through the aftermath of the following showdown or the beginning of the next settlement phase, whichever comes first.

When an event explicitly causes a severe injury or brain trauma, carry its attribute modifiers, impairments, restrictions, and bleeding tokens into the following showdown. An instruction to skip the next hunt refers to the next hunt, not the remainder of the current one. The specific injury or trauma outcome needs its own reviewed source.

The nonlethal exception applies to ordinary hunt-event damage. During a showdown, normal damage beyond armor and available injury boxes can cause a severe injury; brain damage beyond insanity and the brain injury box can cause brain trauma.
